chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Dancers who tried to challenge him
summary: He says Baby Laurence, Eddie Rector, Pops and Louis and others found his dancing too good, citing double-over-the-top and figure-eight.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, did you consider yourself a very competitive dancer?
Were there dancers that tried to challenge you?

Everybody thought they could beat me but when they found out what I was doing they didn't worry about me any more. There weren't many people that could draw against me, no, sir. They knew I was too much then.
Can you name any instances when people did try to come against you?
I had Baby Laurence, I had --
Yeah. I had Eddie Rector and Baby Laurence, I had dancers like Sammy Vanderhurst -- was a dancer. We had Pops and Louis. They all felt that my dancing
was too good for them, you know. They couldn't cope with me.

On what occasion would they have even chosen to -- did you meet them on the street or did you meet them in a rehearsal hall or did you meet them on the back stage. Where would you have met them where they would have even thought of challenging you?

There'd be different dancers that would ask about me. They met the dancers and they'd get together and say, "Oh, did you see John Bubbles dancing? Man, don't bother him. Oh, he's something else. He's got steps that out of this world." I was doing double-over-the-top and figure-eight -- those were the days, you know. When I think about it I says to myself, who would have thought I'd get this far advanced in this thing, you know.
